description: PCB v1.5.3, assembled by JLCPCB (recommended). Upload the gerber, BOM and CPL to JLCPCB and order PCB Assembly. All parts are soldered except the DC-DC, A4988 and Wemos, which are plug-in modules. To save a little, order it without the five 8-pin female headers using this BOM and CPL, and reuse the headers supplied with the modules. Assembly notes. Or buy a ready-made PCB.
Wemos D1 MINI V4.0 (any other version of WeMos that shares the output pins should work)
DC-DC 5V fixed output (no adjustment needed). Choose the single-unit option if available; the price shown is for a 10-pack.
A4988 stepper motor driver+heat sink (It is quite easy to burn it, especially if you are a beginner, better 2 units)
Ultra-slim power supply 100W, 12V or 24V. Choose the same voltage as the hotend. 12V is usually cheaper.
Mini Micro Limit Switch Roller Lever Arm, for strip sensor
Hotend MK8 12V 50W (also available in 24V 40W). It must match the power supply voltage.
Wire 2P 30AWG (for limit switch strip sensor, digital signal, I use the very thin wires stripped from an old LPT1 printer cable)
Wire 2P 18AWG (I use 25cm from the hotend heater cable)
10A 250V Male Power Socket 3 Pin IEC320 switch + Fuse
Terminal Wire Conector Crimp Insulated Ferrule 20AWG (PCB power, IEC320, heater)
Terminal Wire Conector Crimp Insulated Ferrule 24AWG (micro switch)
4.8mm Female Terminal (for the 10A 250V Male Power Socket 3 Pin IEC320)
Heat Shrink Tube 5mm, for strip sensor and 4.8mm Female Terminal
